goal: Restore the MAUI Windows build by applying the targeted CsWinRT workaround for the generated WebView2 type collision.
must_include: Recognizes this as a generated CsWinRT/Windows SDK projection conflict introduced by the Windows toolchain update, not as evidence that the app added WebView2 controls.
Adds `<CsWinRTRcwFactoryFallbackGeneratorForceOptOut>true</CsWinRTRcwFactoryFallbackGeneratorForceOptOut>` in a Windows-only property group.
Keeps the property scoped to the Windows target framework condition instead of affecting Android, iOS, or Mac Catalyst builds.

Recommends cleaning `bin`/`obj` and restoring/building again after changing the project file, and treating the property as a workaround to revisit after updating to serviced .NET MAUI/CsWinRT/Windows App SDK versions.
must_not: Tell them to delete generated files under `obj` as the fix.
Tell them to remove all WebView2 or WinUI references from a MAUI project.
Add `<AllowUnsafeBlocks>true</AllowUnsafeBlocks>` as the primary fix for this WebView2 duplicate-type error.
Apply a Windows SDK package version downgrade globally without explaining that it can introduce other generated-source errors.
acceptable_alternatives: Update to a serviced .NET MAUI/.NET SDK/CsWinRT combination that contains the upstream fix.
Temporarily pin the team to the previous known-good Visual Studio/.NET SDK while applying and validating the targeted project workaround.
solved: The Windows build no longer emits duplicate `CoreWebView2` definitions from `RcwFallbackInitializer.g.cs` and the workaround is scoped to Windows.
partial: The answer identifies the issue family but gives only a broad update/rollback suggestion or applies the property without target-framework scoping.
notes: The source thread reports the exact duplicate WebView2 error after VS 17.11.5 and confirms the fallback-generator opt-out as the targeted workaround.
